description: We are Team Nina Bobo, a multidisciplinary team interested in space exploration, human health, technology, and innovation. Our backgrounds span Astronomy, Engineering Physics, Engineering Management, and Information Systems. We combine scientific thinking, systems analysis, and software development to create NIBO, a sleep recovery and mission-readiness application for astronauts. We interested in UI/UX, AI/ML, data science, software development, and space science to build meaningful solution
summary:
NIBO is an astronaut sleep recovery and mission-readiness support application designed to help astronauts monitor their post-sleep condition and understand how it may affect their ability to perform scheduled mission activities.

Space missions can expose astronauts to challenging sleep conditions, including disrupted circadian rhythms, demanding schedules, and environmental constraints. Insufficient or disrupted sleep may affect alertness, reaction time, cognitive performance, and decision-making.

Unlike conventional health-monitoring systems that primarily display physiological measurements, NIBO connects sleep-related indicators with cognitive performance assessments and mission schedules.

The application combines sleep monitoring, post-wake assessments, personalized reaction-time baselines, and AI-assisted recommendations. It also provides a sleep preparation interface with adjustable cabin lighting and relaxing audio to support a consistent sleep routine.

When potential fatigue-related risks are identified, NIBO can suggest that an astronaut review their scheduled activities and request a task exchange or rescheduling, subject to crew qualifications and mission-control approval.

NIBO aims to transform health monitoring into actionable mission-readiness support.
details:
NIBO: From Better Sleep to Mission Readiness

Project Overview

NIBO (Nina Bobo) is a sleep recovery and mission-readiness support application designed to help astronauts monitor their post-sleep condition and understand how it may affect their ability to perform scheduled mission activities.

Sleep disruption, circadian misalignment, demanding schedules, and environmental constraints can affect astronauts' sleep quality, alertness, and cognitive performance. However, monitoring sleep duration and physiological indicators alone may not fully explain whether an astronaut is prepared for a demanding activity.

NIBO addresses this gap by connecting sleep preparation, post-sleep assessment, health monitoring, and mission scheduling in one integrated platform.

How Does NIBO Work?

NIBO follows four main stages:

1. Sleep Preparation

NIBO provides a sleep preparation interface to help astronauts establish a more consistent sleep routine. It includes:

  • Smart cabin lighting controls to adjust the sleeping environment.
  • Optional relaxing music and audio.
  • Sleep routine reminders and schedule monitoring.

2. Post-Sleep Assessment

After waking up, astronauts can complete an assessment to evaluate their current condition. The application considers:

  • Sleep duration.
  • Reaction time through a Psychomotor Vigilance Test (PVT).
  • Heart rate, when sensor data are available.
  • Self-reported mood and fatigue.

NIBO uses an individual pre-flight reaction-time baseline established through repeated assessments under rested conditions. During the mission, current reaction-time results can be compared against this baseline to identify potential performance changes.

3. AI-Assisted Mission Readiness Assessment

NIBO combines available sleep and health indicators to generate personalized readiness recommendations.

The system aims to identify potential fatigue-related concerns and explain which indicators contribute to its assessment. Its recommendations are categorized into READY, CAUTION, and HOLD.

These results serve as decision-support information rather than medical diagnoses or automatic mission authorization. Final operational decisions remain with authorized medical personnel and mission control.

4. Adaptive Mission Scheduling

If potential concerns are identified, astronauts can request a task exchange with another qualified crew member or request that an activity be rescheduled.

The proposed changes must consider crew qualifications, availability, task dependencies, and operational constraints before receiving mission-control approval.

Benefits and Intended Impact

For astronauts, NIBO provides personalized insights into sleep recovery and daily condition, helping them become more aware of potential changes in their alertness and performance.

For mission operations, NIBO offers additional information to support crew-readiness reviews and provides a structured way to request schedule adjustments when necessary.

Beyond space exploration, the concept could potentially be adapted for occupations that require sustained attention and demanding work schedules, including healthcare workers, pilots, shift workers, and emergency responders.

Our intended impact is to move beyond passive health monitoring toward actionable, human-centered decision support.

Creativity and Innovation

NIBO's main innovation is its integration of sleep recovery monitoring with mission-readiness assessment and adaptive scheduling.

Instead of simply displaying sleep statistics or physiological measurements, NIBO connects an astronaut's recovery condition with their upcoming operational responsibilities.

Three elements distinguish our approach:

  • Personalized performance monitoring: Reaction-time results are compared against an individual's pre-flight baseline rather than relying exclusively on generic population averages.
  • Recovery-to-readiness connection: Sleep information and post-wake performance assessments are combined to provide more meaningful insights.
  • Actionable scheduling support: Health-related concerns can lead to a request for task exchange or rescheduling, connecting personal well-being with mission operations.

This creates a continuous workflow:

Sleep Preparation → Post-Sleep Assessment → Mission Readiness Assessment → Adaptive Scheduling

Factors Considered

During the development of NIBO, our team considered several important factors:

  • Human factors: Astronauts need an accessible interface that does not create unnecessary cognitive workload.
  • Scientific validity: Sleep and reaction-time indicators should be interpreted using established research principles.
  • Individual differences: Each astronaut has different physiological characteristics and baseline performance.
  • Operational feasibility: Scheduling recommendations must respect crew qualifications, mission priorities, and task dependencies.
  • Data availability: Recommendations should account for missing or unavailable sensor measurements.
  • Safety and privacy: NIBO is intended to support, not replace, professional medical assessment and mission-control decisions.

Tools and Technologies

NIBO is developed as a web-based application.

Development tools and technologies include:

  • Frontend: CSS, Javascript, Typescript
  • Backend: Python
  • AI/Data Processing: Codex
  • UI/UX Design: Figma
  • Version Control: GitHub

The prototype demonstrates the proposed user experience and workflow. Features that require physical cabin hardware, live physiological sensors, or validated predictive models may require further integration and testing.

Future Development

Future development could include integration with wearable devices, more extensive validation of personal reaction-time baselines, improved circadian rhythm modeling, and direct integration with mission scheduling systems.

Our vision is to make NIBO a human-centered platform that connects astronaut recovery, cognitive performance, and mission operations.

NIBO — Better Recovery. Smarter Decisions. Safer Missions.
